Anika Review

Pros

  • High buffing capabilities with Neutral epiphanies.

  • Provides a strong source of Tenacity Damage. 

  • Flexible playstyle, can be played as either a Carry or Support.

Cons

  • If playing as a support, teams may suffer from sustain as Anika doesn’t have any healing.

  • Doesn’t provide much card draw.

Review

Introduction

Anika is the first post-release 4-Star combatant, an Order-Attribute Striker combatant that hacks, slashes and blasts their enemies away with their gunsword. 

Anika is a Support combatant who utilizes Lead cards. Many of Anika’s cards feature the Efficiency: tag that grants additional effects if the card has its cost reduced, counting cost-reduction Divines. Anika also provides additive damage buffs and additional Tenacity Damage via their Shockwave debuff.

Review

Key Mechanics

  • Efficiency

    • Efficiency is an additional effect that activates when a card is activated and in a Cost-Reduced state, such as either through the Lead tag or potentially even via Cost-Reducing Divine Epiphanies.

  • Shockwave

    • Shockwave is a debuff that lasts a single turn and causes the enemy inflicted with Shockwave to take double Tenacity Damage from cards, additionally when the enemy inflicted is in a Ravaged state, they take an additional +50% damage when dealt damage.

  • Stampede

    • +5% Damage Amount to ally Attack Cards and apply 2x that amount for Anika. At the end of the turn, remove effect (max 5 stacks)

  • Hand-Lock

    • For 1 turn, cannot move or Draw cards to hand (except for Turn Draw)

Deck uses Anika as the main buffer for Anika, Hugo, and Chizuru on-top of providing one additional Extra Attack for every Chizuru Moonslash. This effectively means the team gains an additional Extra Attack for every Chizuru BA on-top of Hugo's existing 2, which makes it so Chizuru is now doing 5 hits (2 normal, 3 EA) for every Basic Attack, turning her into a vastly more competitive driver than previous iterations of the team, with the main drawback being a lack of sustain.

This is not an exhaustive list of teams this deck can be used in, merely examples pooled from Team Database to reference as a launch board.

Teams Database

  • Hugo Driver (Chizuru - Anika Variant)

Synergies

Anika Synergies

Sereniel
Ravage DPS

Anika is able to buff Sereniel more than alternative options and works well with Sereniel's low Draw needs in her teams, making her a competitive option versus buffers like Cassius especially for modes where Cassius cannot be played on the team because of other team commitments.

  • Gives a lot of AP to be able to play high cost neutral morale Anika cards and maximize Anika buffs.
  • Generally requires low amount of Draw, which can get around Anika not offering Draw for allies.
  • Can capitalize on Tenacity and Ravage based buffs because of Sereniel's Ravage playstyle.
Veronica
Draw Support

Because Anika's main drawback is lack of Draw support, Veronica can effectively cover this to make Anika more of a competitive option with many hypercarries.

  • Can alleviate Draw issues, which Anika often experiences for both her premiere buffing and damage builds.
  • With Rosaria, Veronica can cap out Morale at high odds in Anika’s generic buffing build because of Anika getting close to cap alone but not exactly.
  • Together, they offer no sustain if not using a Shield Veronica setup.
Chizuru
Basic Attack Spammer

When sustain is not an issue, Anika can enable much higher efficiency on Chizuru raising her cap as a driver a rather substantial amount versus previous iterations.

  • Is able to utilize Anika’s epiphany that turns Anika into an Extra Attacker for Basic Attack spammers better than most alternatives.
  • Needs to be ran alongside Hugo to be worth it but then the team is almost sustainless (only Chizuru's healing).
Mei Lin
Basic Attack Spammer

When sustain is not an issue, Anika can enable much higher efficiency on Chizuru raising her cap as a driver a rather substantial amount versus previous iterations but suffers from a variety of AP and Draw concerns.

  • Is able to utilize Anika’s epiphany that turns Anika into an Extra Attacker for Basic Attack spammers better than most alternatives.
  • Clunkier to use than Chizuru but technically a bit higher cap (can do 2 more Basic Attacks but is much more expensive).
  • Only worth it in sustainless teams (Mei + Selena + Anika), which is another loss compared to Chizuru for Anika as Chizuru at least has some sustain.

Anika memory fragments are extremely flexible, with it being recommended to take options to improve tankiness like Healer's Journey, but it being completely acceptable to opt for damage alternatives. It's important to note that Memory Fragments do not affect Sortie currently so building her DPS will not improve her performance in Sortie.
Main Stats

Anika Stats

Ideal

Crit Rate > Crit DMG

Desire

ATK% >= Order DMG%

Imagination

ATK%

Substats

CRIT DMG% > CRIT Rate% => Extra DMG% > ATK > ATK%

Maxing out Anika's potential 7 is the main stat breakpoint to watch out for. Fortunately, it's incredibly easy to do so, and all you need is 500ATK which Anika builds can accomplish with no memory fragments.
Investment

Anika Potential Priority

CRIT RATE% = CRIT DMG% >= Unique Card DMG% > Common Card DMG% = Basic Card DMG%

  • 3-1: Anika’s 3-1 Potential adds the [Lead] tag to both of their basic starting cards, Blaster Swing and Position Hold cards. Mostly useful for early in Chaos/Sortie runs to slightly help alleviate AP requirements. 
  • 5-1: Anika’s 5-1 Potential adds an additional +5% Damage to their Blaster Swing card, improving to 15% total if Anika’s attack is 250 or higher. Again, primarily serving useful early in Chaos/Sortie prior to removal.
  • 7: Anika’s 7 Potential grants Anika an additional +10% Attack to their attack stat if their attack is 500 or higher. Very strong, should be prioritized as this increases their damage across the board.

Seasonal

Anika Seasonal Powers

Introduces Desire Cards. Desire Cards are cards that primarily exist to give a strong passive buff from meeting certain Desire Thresholds (3/5/7) which can only be done by having multiple ally decks also made in Season-4. 

  • For Desire Threshold, it’s common to run 1 Claim / 1 Survival / 1 Inquiry for use in a variety of builds on supports; however, it's also common to just do 3 ‘X’ to meet effect easier or do 2 'X' / 1 Inquiry (to keep Sample Collection as Card Effect). This is extremely dependent on ally desire cards and individual team building goal.

’X’ refers to a ‘Placeholder for Specific Desire Threshold Goal’, i.e. if you are building your team for 7 Claim then you might do 2 Claim / 1 Inquiry.

Introduces Persona Cards and Engravings. Persona Cards are powerful cards that introduce new playstyles or ways of buffing/debuffing. Engravings are effects that can be applied to both the Persona Cards and Equipment, functioning near identically to Refinements of Season-2 but with new effects.

  • The most common Card Engraving to take is Attunement: Decrease Cost by 1 until used].

  • The most common Equipment Engraving to optimize for is the stacking [When Action Count of enemies is increased by allies, +50% Damage Amount to Ally Attack Cards for 1 turn (1 time per turn)] and [When a card of this unit is activated, 30% to increase Action Count of all enemies by 1 (1 time per turn)], but it's possible to use a variety of other options for a specific set-up (like Discard [Quietus] Engravings when playing high [Quietus] builds or Umbra Engravings just to meet the threshold for certain Persona cards).

Introduces Refinements, effects on Equipment that allow one to get additional Equipment effects for no Faint-Cost (post-S2), and God’s Hammer, a powerful effect that gives a random copy of any other Equipment effect on-top of current Equipment but costs 10 Faint Memory and is only gained from the Boss. 

  • At the start of battle, Draw 1 Exhaust card(s) of this unit.

  • At the start of the turn, if an Exhaust card is in Draw Pile, have a 30% chance to Draw 1 Exhaust card(s).

  • If Damage is completely blocked, at the start of the next turn, increase Damage Amount of allies by 10% for 1 turn (1 time per turn).

  • When Drawing an Exhaust card of this unit through an ally ability, activate immediately (1 time per turn).

Because God’s Hammer is completely RNG at the end of the run, we do not have a specific recommendation since the player has very little control over the decision. Supportive options are recommended for supportive units (like Tentacle or Harp effects).

Introduces Forbidden Cards, powerful cards that create new synergies and can only be acquired once per run (can be duped at one event or via save data editing). 

  • Forbidden: Gesture of Freedom. Permanent Cost-Reduction to 1-card, can be manipulated.

  • Forbidden: Eternal Hunger. +Draw, ++AP (Ally Reliant)

  • Forbidden: Portrait of Fury. ++Draw

  • Forbidden: Guidance of Futility. +++Survivability

[Target Neutral Epiphany: 3 Morale]

This card is a rare case of Neutral epiphanies being generally preferable to specific epiphanies; thus, it is recommended to ignore normal epiphanies and build 3 Morale. This is largely because Anika's own buffs do not stack as favorably as Morale nor are they as strong, and Anika's Efficiency mechanic enables higher Morale generation than most competitors.

[General Role]

Ignition Slash deals upfront damage to a single enemy and inflicts heavy Tenacity Damage, while also granting AP if used in a Cost-Reduced state. Ignition Slash’s various epiphanies don’t drastically change the card, outside of Ignition Slash V - Base Ignition Slash with a Morale Neutral Epiphany will be the most viable option.

[Special Notes]

Ignition Slash V offers some synergy with Basic Attack units, can considered if pairing Anika with units who can use their Basic-Attack cards multiple times per turn.
